deliverables: WP1: Plutarch and Ply Maintenance, Compatibility & Developer Experience
Bug fixes, correctness improvements, and optimizations
Documentation, examples, technical blog posts, and developer-experience improvements
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor MLabs
request.what: Annual funding for MLabs Core Tool Maintenance & Enhancement: Plutarch and Ply, including maintenance, compatibility, bug fixes, optimizations, documentation, and developer-experience improvements.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,162,746 ada, consisting of 1,128,880 ada for Plutarch and Ply maintenance, compatibility, and developer experience plus a 33,866 ada Intersect administration fee.

Plutarch is described as a Haskell eDSL for creating efficient Cardano smart contracts through controlled compilation into UPLC, and Ply is described as tooling for serializing Plutarch scripts to and from CIP-57 blueprint-style artifacts with inferred types.

MLabs states that Plutarch and Ply have been extensively used in the Cardano ecosystem and reports an internal audit count of at least 26 teams in one section and at least 15 teams in another section.
MLabs claims its public cross-language benchmarks show Plutarch scripts rank among the smallest in the benchmark suite while requiring comparatively low on-chain compute and memory.

The proposal says funded work will prioritize critical breakages and vulnerabilities, protocol-era and hard-fork compatibility, bug fixes and optimizations, and documentation and developer-experience improvements in that order.

The proposer claims continued maintenance is crucial because if Plutarch and Ply fall behind ledger and Plutus/UPLC evolution, existing adopters may face friction, migration risk, workarounds, rewrites, or expensive stack migrations.

The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The proposal states the requested amount did not, at submission, breach the applicable 350M ada Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713, either alone or in aggregate.

The proposal states Intersect will manage funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with a TRSC, a PSSC, defined multisignature-style permissions, an Oversight Committee, reporting obligations, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard.

The proposal discloses prior MLabs funding through prior governance actions, Project Catalyst Fund9 and Fund13 awards, and a previous 70,000 ada Intersect payment to update Plutarch for Conway-era features.

summary: The document requests 1,162,746 ada for MLabs Plutarch and Ply maintenance through Intersect-managed treasury contracts, citing ecosystem usage, technical performance, protocol compatibility needs, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, oversight arrangements, and prior funding disclosures.
